MAKE.01.note: The ACS review explains the Maillard reaction as a network beginning with reducing sugars and amino groups and producing aromas, colours and texture changes that depend strongly on heat, water activity and pH.

article.title: Control of Maillard Reactions in Foods: Strategies and Chemical Mechanisms
article.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry — ACS

exercise.prompt: Brown identical onion or bread samples under different moisture, temperature and pH conditions, then compare colour, aroma, texture and time to browning.

MAKE.02.note: University of Minnesota Extension distinguishes lactic-acid, yeast and other food fermentations while emphasizing salt, acidity, oxygen control, temperature and safe handling.

exercise.prompt: Plan a vegetable fermentation with ingredient mass, salt percentage, temperature, oxygen exclusion, pH checks, spoilage signs and a discard rule.

MAKE.03.note: The ACS material explains chocolate manufacture through cocoa-butter crystallisation, heating, cooling and controlled formation of the stable crystal structure responsible for gloss and snap.

article.title: The Chemistry of Romance, Flavor, and Drink: Roses, Chocolate, and Wine

exercise.prompt: Temper one batch correctly and let another cool without seeding or temperature control, then compare gloss, snap, contraction, texture and fat bloom over several days.

MAKE.04.note: The Specialty Coffee Association connects brew ratio, total dissolved solids and extraction yield, correcting the oversimple rule that sour always means under-extracted and bitter always means over-extracted.

exercise.prompt: Brew the same coffee at three grind sizes while holding dose and water constant, record brew time and taste, and separate strength from extraction balance.

MAKE.05.note: The research explains how gliadin-rich and glutenin-rich protein mixtures produce different viscous, elastic and strain-hardening behaviour underlying dough extensibility and strength.

article.title: Flow of Gluten with Tunable Protein Composition: From Stress Undershoot to Stress Overshoot and Strain Hardening

exercise.prompt: Mix and wash a small dough to isolate gluten, then compare development after short mixing, intensive mixing and resting using stretch, windowpane and gas-retention tests.

MAKE.06.note: Penn State's guide reduces cheesemaking to its controlling decisions: milk treatment, starter culture, acidification, rennet coagulation, curd cutting, cooking, draining, salting and ageing.

exercise.prompt: Create a decision tree showing how acid versus rennet coagulation, curd size, cooking, pressing, salt, moisture, rind organisms and ageing produce different cheese families.

MAKE.07.note: The Scotch Whisky Association traces malting, mashing, fermentation, distillation and oak maturation and distinguishes legal requirements from marketing mythology.

exercise.prompt: Trace starch to bottled whisky and mark where enzymes, yeast, still shape, cut points, oak extraction, oxidation, evaporation and blending alter the final spirit.

MAKE.08.note: The Met distinguishes pattern welding—forge-welded bars arranged and twisted for structure and pattern—from crucible or watered steels often grouped loosely under the Damascus label.

article.title: Techniques of Decoration on Arms and Armor

exercise.prompt: Diagram a pattern-welded billet through stacking, forge welding, drawing, twisting, cutting and restacking, then contrast it with historical crucible steel.

MAKE.09.note: The American Ceramic Society connects glassblowing craft to viscosity, temperature control, thermal expansion, annealing and the non-crystalline structure of glass.

article.title: Scientific Glassblowing—Part Science, Part Art, All Awesome

exercise.prompt: Plot a qualitative glass-working temperature curve and mark gathering, blowing, shaping, strain point, annealing and the risks of uneven cooling.

MAKE.10.note: The American Ceramic Society introduces ceramics as inorganic non-metallic materials and provides the materials-science foundation for clay transformation, sintering and glassy glaze layers.

exercise.prompt: Create a kiln schedule and materials map for one glazed clay body, identifying water loss, burnout, quartz change, sintering, vitrification, glaze melting and cooling defects.

MAKE.11.note: Japan's only museum devoted to carpentry tools presents timber selection, marking, hand tools, post-and-beam framing, joinery and the repairable traditions of temple and tea-house construction.

exercise.prompt: Model a mortise-and-tenon or scarf joint from card or soft wood and identify the surfaces resisting tension, compression, shear, rotation and withdrawal.

MAKE.12.note: The Met explains natural-dye practice through fibres, mordants and the unusual reduction-oxidation chemistry that makes insoluble indigo enter cloth and turn blue in air.

article.title: The Materials and Techniques of American Quilts and Coverlets

exercise.prompt: Draw the indigo vat cycle from insoluble pigment through chemical reduction, dissolved leuco-indigo, fibre uptake, air oxidation and repeated dipping for depth.
